policy_direction_of_yea: supports discretionary and transferable tariff tax credits for industrial projects investing at least $100 million and creating at least 100 qualifying jobs
human_review_note: Targeted-industrial-policy and large-project-subsidy anchor. Do not interpret as generic pro-business or free-market conservatism.

policy_direction_of_yea: removes protected funding for the Tutwiler women's prison and permits reallocation within the corrections system
human_review_note: Marginally conservative social-justice signal: supporters emphasized administrative flexibility, while opponents emphasized vulnerable inmates, federal scrutiny, facility conditions, and legislative accountability.

policy_direction_of_yea: removes a facility-specific corrections earmark and expands ADOC discretion to allocate existing funds during the General Fund crisis
human_review_note: Conservative budget signal favoring administrative flexibility, fewer earmarks, and management of the budget shortfall without relying entirely on new taxes.

policy_direction_of_yea: supports and constitutionally validates a discretionary program allowing approved companies to retain a portion of employee income-tax withholding for qualifying job-creation and retention projects
human_review_note: Targeted-industrial-policy anchor based on HB159 and its companion HB160. Yea favors state-directed incentives and executive flexibility; Nay is ideologically ambiguous. Do not interpret as generic pro-business or assign a simple liberal-conservative score.

policy_direction_of_yea: requires a municipality or municipal public authority abating county taxes for economic development to abate the corresponding municipal tax at the same rate
human_review_note: Secondary, marginally conservative local-fiscal-restraint signal. Yea favors fiscal symmetry and intergovernmental accountability but does not indicate general opposition to industrial incentives.

policy_direction_of_yea: expands long-term ad valorem and construction-related transaction-tax abatements for qualifying data centers and logistics facilities while reducing the data-center employment threshold
human_review_note: Targeted-industrial-policy anchor. The act permits sector-specific abatements lasting up to 30 years, preserves education taxes, establishes capital and employment thresholds, and prevents certain replacement jobs from being counted as new employment. Do not assign a simple liberal-conservative score.

policy_direction_of_yea: prohibits governmental entities from using covered public contracts or other governmental pressure to advance economic boycotts targeting a bundle of protected industries, environmental and corporate-governance choices, firearms activity, and refusals to facilitate abortion or gender-transition care
human_review_note: Bundled conservative anti-ESG governance anchor. Suitable as an overall ideological signal, but do not use it as a clean position on any single component issue or infer that the legislator separately endorsed every protected activity.

policy_direction_of_yea: redirects all dedicated scrap-tire environmental-fee revenue to the State General Fund for fiscal years 2013 and 2014
human_review_note: Conservative budget-priority signal favoring temporary General Fund flexibility over dedicated fee revenue. The normal allocation formula resumed beginning October 1, 2014.

policy_direction_of_yea: suspends dedicated funding for scrap-tire remediation, environmental enforcement, county programs, and recycling-market development for two fiscal years
human_review_note: Narrow environmental-priority signal. Treat as a temporary funding tradeoff during fiscal pressure, not evidence of broad opposition to environmental regulation.

policy_direction_of_yea: requires more frequent electronic campaign-finance reporting, expands reporting requirements for Section 527 organizations and large contributions, and establishes a state electronic disclosure database

policy_direction_of_yea: requires disclosure to the Ethics Commission of the names and compensation of public officials and their spouses who are employed by or contract with the state or a local government

policy_direction_of_yea: expands the category of minor ethics violations eligible for consent-based administrative resolution, raises the maximum administrative fine from $1,000 to $6,000, and makes an approved administrative resolution preclude later state or local criminal prosecution

policy_direction_of_yea: requires all covered campaign-finance reports to be filed electronically without the prior exceptions
